response: Ultrasound imaging before puncture does not necessarily facilitate internal jugular vein cannulation in all cases. According to the available data, prepuncture ultrasound evaluation did not improve the result of right internal jugular vein cannulation compared to the respiratory jugular venodilation-guided approach. However, when the landmark was not observed, prepuncture ultrasound guidance was found to be helpful in facilitating the cannulation. This suggests that ultrasound imaging can be a useful tool in certain situations, but it may not be universally necessary or beneficial for internal jugular vein cannulation.
